rv.q: Invictus Theatre Company’s penetrating and profound new presentation is excellent.
“Network” is a fantastic production, with convincing lights-camera-action of a television station, and even the audience called into the action.
Invictus has crafted a memorable production of an important and illuminating play.
Invictus' Network is a powerful play, highlighting just how much we've lost ourselves in the years since all of this could reasonably be seen as satire.
James Turano as Howard Beale is the real deal. A WGN Radio regular, he convincingly channels Beale's anguish, rage, and dynamism into the role.
Invictus Theatre of Chicago's production of 'Network' is stunning, immersive and unforgettable.

cn.t: Critics praise this powerhouse Chicago production as timely and thrilling, with Lee Hall's adaptation of the 1976 film proving even more resonant today. The raw, full-throttle staging delivers excitement and emotional punch.
